html:
The Angolan Civil War was fought from 1975 to 2002 between the MPLA government and the UNITA rebels of Jonas Savimbi, with long breaks in fighting, and was one of the main proxy wars of the Cold War.

The Soviet Union and tens of thousands of Cuban troops backed the government, while South Africa and the United States backed UNITA. The war peaked at Cuito Cuanavale in 1987 and 1988. Agreements in 1988 sent the Cubans home, and Namibia became independent.

A peace in 1991 led to elections in 1992, but Savimbi rejected the results and war resumed, paid for by oil on one side and diamonds on the other. It ended weeks after Savimbi was killed in February 2002. Hundreds of thousands died, and millions of landmines were left in Angola, a legacy of the Cold War.
sum: The Angolan Civil War was fought from 1975 to 2002 between the MPLA government and the UNITA rebels of Jonas Savimbi, with long breaks in fighting, and was one of the main proxy wars of the Cold War.
